Black-box test `$1` against a running app and write a findings report. Verify only — never fix
the code, and never present a fix as done.

Arguments: `$1` is the feature or bug report to verify; `$2` is an optional base URL.
Read `./aw.config.json` for the rest (`app.baseUrl`, `app.backend`, `app.testAccount`,
`app.stagingUrl`, `offLimits`). If `$1` is empty, stop and ask for a description — that is the
only question this command may ask.

PLAYWRIGHT MCP IS REQUIRED for every browser step. Before the first one, check that the
`mcp__playwright__browser_*` tools are available. If they are not, STOP and tell the developer
to run `claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest` and restart Claude Code
(docs/HANDOFF.md Step 1). Never substitute curl, a headless script or a described screenshot
for a real browser check.

1. **Target.** `$2` if given, else `app.baseUrl`, else `http://localhost:<app.backend.port>`.
   If none of those exist, stop with `no target: pass a base URL or configure app.baseUrl`.
2. **Safety.** If the target is not localhost/127.0.0.1 it MUST equal `app.stagingUrl` exactly —
   otherwise stop and print both values. Never touch production, not even with a probe.
   POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE against a non-local target need the developer's explicit confirmation in
   this session before you send them; against localhost they are allowed. Respect `offLimits`.
3. **Reachability.** Probe `<target><app.backend.healthPath ?? "/">` (5 s). If it is down and
   `app.backend.start` is configured for that same host and port, start it in the background from
   the repo root, poll every 2 s for up to 60 s, and stop it again when the run ends. Then the two
   cases part company, exactly as the CLI does:
   - you started it and it never answered — stop there with the command you tried, the repo root
     and the last error. No report: an app that will not boot is not a test result.
   - there was no start command for that host and port — test the target as given. The refused
     connections ARE the result: record each exact failed request and mark the cases FAIL, then
     go on to step 6 and write the report.
   Either way, do not hunt for the app on another port and do not test any other address.
4. **Plan and execute.** Delegate to the **qa-tester** subagent (Task). Give it the description,
   the target, whether destructive methods are permitted, the test-account user and the env var
   holding the password (never the password itself), and `offLimits`. It must first write a plan
   covering happy path, edge cases, invalid input and authn/authz — for a bug report, the exact
   repro steps — then run every case with a real call before grading it. Throwaway files go under
   `test-reports/tmp/` only (screenshots as
   `test-reports/tmp/screenshots/<screen>-<viewport>.png`); application source is never modified.
5. **Collect.** Every case comes back as `{ id, name, kind (happy|edge|invalid|auth),
   status (PASS|FAIL|SKIP), request, response, reproSteps?, severity? }`. `request` and `response`
   are mandatory for every FAIL and must be the literal text that was seen; `severity`
   (BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR|NIT) is for FAIL cases only. If the answer is unusable, ask once more for
   the case list alone — no second full run.
6. **Report.** Write `test-reports/<slug>-<date>.md`, where `<slug>` is the description
   lowercased and hyphenated (≤ 80 chars) and `<date>` is today in local time
   as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
   Never overwrite an existing report — append `-2`, `-3`, … Sections, in order:
   a title line `# Test report — <description>`; a bullet list with **Target**, **Agent**,
   **Run at** (ISO 8601) and the PASS/FAIL/SKIP counts, plus **App started by this run** when you
   started it; `## Test plan`; `## Cases` with one `### <n>. <name> — <STATUS>` block per case
   (id, kind, severity, fenced Request, fenced Response, repro steps); `## Summary` (≤ 3 lines).
7. **Present.** Print the report path, then the ≤ 3-line summary, then `PASS <passed>/<total>`.
   Failing cases are findings, not a broken run. Stop there and wait for the developer.
